sources.title: "Simone Weil: Voluntary Worker" (JSTOR Daily) -- documents her 1934-1935 factory labor experiment
Simone Weil entry, Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
Weil's own Factory Journal and her London-period work The Need for Roots

independent_thinking.rationale: Three independent, decades-spanning documented instances of translating philosophical conviction directly into personal action rather than abstract theorizing: took unpaid leave from teaching to become an unskilled factory laborer, insisting on living on the actual factory wage (1934-1935); joined an armed anarchist militia at the Spanish Civil War front (1936); and deliberately restricted her own food intake in 1943 to match the ration levels available to French civilians under occupation.

risk_tolerance.rationale: Two independent, high-stakes documented instances of accepting real personal risk and hardship for principle: voluntarily became an unskilled factory laborer living on factory wages alone specifically to experience industrial workers' real material conditions, and joined an armed anarchist militia at the Spanish Civil War front, where she sustained a serious foot and ankle burn injury in a camp accident.

conflict_tolerance.rationale: Sustained political activism on behalf of factory workers, peasants, and colonized people while employed as a secondary-school teacher across multiple institutions (1931-1937), drawing repeated documented institutional criticism for this activism, a sustained willingness to remain in institutional friction rather than moderate her public positions.

belief_updating.rationale: Traveled to Barcelona in 1936 hoping a genuine working-class revolution was underway, but after direct front-line observation over several weeks concluded that the atmosphere of civil war itself was "fatal to the ideals for which the war was being fought" -- a genuine, reasoned revision of her initial position based on direct evidence rather than continued adherence to her prior hope.

cross_domain_range.rationale: Sustained substantial, independently-verifiable activity across teaching, industrial manual labor, armed political conflict, and formal wartime governmental planning work (preparing reports on France's post-war reconstruction for the Free French movement in London, 1942-1943), all within roughly a decade -- genuinely distinct domains, not variations on one theme.
